title: simple-dispatcher: clean main gives a clean test run on the runner host
description:
Repo: **JKershaw/simple-dispatcher**.

## Why

On the runner host, the unit suite fails on untouched `main`. A Survey on 3 Nov counted 46 failures caused by the machine, not the code (the leak-trap census paths, the git launch probe, the fake-opencode spawns), and the system suite fails differently on `main` than on a branch. So every builder has to diff their failing names against a baseline before they can trust a result. Three builders did that by hand on 3 Nov (LIN-4165, LIN-4171, LIN-4172).

## What we want

A builder on the host can tell their change's failures from the host's at a glance: clean `main` gives a clean, trustworthy run there. A test that genuinely can't run on this machine says why, rather than failing. Nothing that guards real behaviour is weakened to get there.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

A Survey looked at the ground first. Its advice, which we're taking:

* **First, establish the baseline, because it depends on where you run from.** At the same commit, the Survey saw 1 failure in a workspace clone, 4 in a `/tmp` worktree, and 119 with `TMPDIR` inside the checkout's `state/` (this host puts session temp folders there). Post that table on this ticket. Say where builders should run, and where the "46" came from if you can find out.
* **Then fix the harness, not the tests.** The Survey's reading: the test isolation pins the state folder and temp root, but not the workspace clone root, which follows the checkout's location. And the run root can land inside `state/`, where every sandboxed write counts as a leak. Don't widen the shared roots or exempt paths per test, and keep the leak-trap tests green. Keep the run root out of `state/` rather than teaching the classifier to ignore it.
* **One test checks the host rather than the code:** the git launch probe, which asserts that the host's broken git is still broken. Make it check its precondition and skip with a stated reason, and keep its injected cases.
* **Then re-run everything, the system suite included,** and post the after table.

## Implementation Plan

*Implemented and merged; the plan body was pruned at close-out.* Shipped as the plan said (D1 clone root pinned in the preload, D2 run root kept out of `state/`, D3 git probe checks its precondition and skips with a reason, D4 docs), in [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/309](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/309>) (squash `11a1279`). Deviations: the review added two fixes, `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT` so the LIN-558 guard is not made vacuous by the pin, and a reaper (`test/system/harness/reap.js`) so a killed or timed-out system test file cannot orphan a Harbour server. The four system-suite failures were triaged as not host-related and are tracked in LIN-4185, LIN-4186, LIN-4187 and LIN-4188. The baseline table, the after-tables, the review and the close-out are in the comment trail; the full pre-prune description is kept in the task snapshots.

* **fits one session.**
* plan-review due: no (test-harness and one test precondition; no credentials, merge rules, dispatch contract; nothing guard-loosening: the trap's rules and shared roots are unchanged and the only skipped case is the host-checking one).

comments.body:
### Baseline (planner, HEAD 600f1be, Node v25.9.0) — `npm test`
| Run location | tests | fail | cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. workspace clone, session TMPDIR | 3831 | 1 | git-launch-probe host precondition |
| B. checkout under /tmp, default TMPDIR | 3834 | 4 (+704 leaks) | clone root `<checkout>/../simple-dispatcher-workspaces` is in shared /tmp |
| C. TMPDIR inside the checkout's `state/` | 3934 | 119 (~8900 leaks) | run root `sd-test-run-*` lands inside `state/` |

`npm run test:system` (HARBOUR_DIR = sibling LinearViewer @ 9e397e6b): A 117 tests / 4 fail (deterministic over two runs; not shown to be host noise); B 129 tests / 16 fail (= the same 4 + 12 files hit by the /tmp clone-root leak).

The "46" could not be traced: no location gives it, and LIN-4165/4171/4172 only record the 1 git-probe failure. Where to run today: A. After the fix, anywhere. Plan is in the description.

**LIN-4181: PR open, CI green.** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/309 (branch `feat/lin-4181-clean-main-test-run`, commit `eb167d8`)

**What changed (fix at the cause, no test or trap rule relaxed)**
- **Clone root pinned:** the preload always sets `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT=<run root>/workspaces`, overriding a shell value.
- **Run root never in `state/`:** it goes under the host tmpdir, or `/tmp` (then home) when the tmpdir is inside the protected state dir. The check and the trap now share `test/protected-paths.js`.
- **Git probe checks its precondition:** the live case skips with the observed git resolution as its reason when git works, and runs (must refuse) when the fault is present. Injected cases unchanged.
- **Docs:** `docs/testing-and-ci.md` covers the pins, the skip rule and the baseline method.

**Unit suite (`npm test`), after**
| Location | Before | After |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A. workspace clone, session TMPDIR | 3831 tests, 1 fail | 3837, 0 fail, 5 skipped (each with a reason) |
| B. checkout under `/tmp` | 3834, 4 fail, 704 leaks | 3837, 0 fail, 0 leaks |
| C. TMPDIR inside `state/` | 119 fail, ~8900 leaks | 3837, 0 fail, 0 leaks |

**System suite (`npm run test:system`)**
- A: 117 tests, 4 fail, identical on `main` and the branch: `halt-mechanism`, `harbour-halt`, `observation-feed`, `tap1-openrouter`. Harbour-state assertions, not path or host causes. Not triaged to one cause, so not changed here; name them as known-failing and file one ticket per cause.
- B and C: not measurable right now. Another workspace's `node server.js` processes hold the suite's fixed ports 4124–4161 on this host (`EADDRINUSE`/`ECONNREFUSED` in both `main` and branch logs). Re-measure once those ports are free.

**Witnesses:** two new `isolate-run` cases failed red before the change and pass after; the live git case was forced to run on this host and failed with the original refusal assertion, then restored.

## Review — LIN-4181

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/309, head `eb167d8` (base `600f1be`; `main` is now `0992f39`, and the PR merges onto it cleanly).

CI: green on `eb167d8` ("unit tests", Linux). I also re-ran the suite myself on this host (below).

### What was checked
- **Scope matches the plan.** D1 (clone root pinned), D2 (run root kept out of `state/`, with one shared `test/protected-paths.js`), D3 (the git probe checks its precondition first) and D4 (docs) touch only the six files listed. The trap's rules and shared roots are unchanged. The injected git-probe cases and `git-launch-probe-process.test.js` are unchanged.
- **Regression history:** `git log` on the touched files shows LIN-4077, LIN-2509, LIN-3160, LIN-4171 and LIN-4180. Nothing is reverted or re-applied. The `canon()` move keeps the same algorithm. It now calls `fs.realpathSync` when it runs, not a copy saved at load. That is safe because the trap does not wrap `realpathSync` and no test stubs it.
- **Mutation checks (each change undone afterwards):**
  - M1, run root put back under the original tmpdir: `puts the run root outside the protected state dir` fails.
  - M2, `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT` pin commented out: `pins WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT inside the run root` fails.
  - M3, the precondition skip forced off on this host: the live probe case fails with the original refusal assertion.
  - M4, exit status 0 treated as the fault: the `liveGitPrecondition` unit case and the live case both fail.
  All four tests catch the change they claim to cover.
- **Unit suite, run by me (Node v25.9.0, host git `/opt/homebrew/bin/git` 2.46.0):**

| Run | tests | fail | skip | leaks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A, `main` @0992f39 | 3853 | **1** (git probe live case) | 4 | 0 |
| A, PR @eb167d8 | 3837 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| A, PR merged onto 0992f39 | 3859 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| B, PR checkout in `/private/tmp`, default per-user TMPDIR | 3837 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| C, PR merged, TMPDIR inside `state/` | 3859 | 0 | 5 | 0 |

  Every skip gives a reason. The new one is `login shell resolves git to /opt/homebrew/bin/git, which works; the Apple shim fault is not present on this host`.

### Finding (blocking): the pin makes an existing guard pass without checking anything
`test/workspace-clones.test.js:35-42`, *"resolves outside the dispatcher repo (no ancestor CLAUDE.md leaks into a clone)"* (LIN-558), starts with `if (process.env.WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT) return;`. D1 now sets that variable on every `npm test`, in CI too, so this guard always returns before asserting. **Mutation:** I changed `config.js`'s default clone root to `path.join(__dirname, 'state', 'workspaces')`, which is the exact regression LIN-558 fixed. On `main` with the preload the test fails. On the PR it passes (16/16). This breaks the ticket's rule that nothing which guards real behaviour is weakened. It is caused by this PR's own change and lives in this ticket's bounded class (D1 / test-run paths), so it is **inside** scope.
**Fix:** in `config.js`, export `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT = path.join(path.dirname(__dirname), 'simple-dispatcher-workspaces')` and define `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT = process.env.WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT || DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`. In the test, delete the early `return` and assert on `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`. **Witness:** the same mutation must turn the test red under `npm test`.
A search for other tests that return early on an env var the preload sets (`WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`, `SD_STATE_DIR`, `TMPDIR`, `SD_TEST_RUN_ROOT`) found no others, so this one is isolated.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside (D1 / guard not weakened):** the LIN-558 guard above. CI is green because the guard no longer checks anything. Settle it before merge with the fix and the witness above.
- **Inside (plan step 4, "re-run everything, the system suite included"):** `npm run test:system` in B and C has still not been measured. My A run on the PR (Harbour `LinearViewer` @`10b2c82f`) was contaminated too: 2 files failed, there were 16 `EADDRINUSE`/`ECONNREFUSED` errors, and several files hit 300 s timeouts. The cause is two orphaned `node server.js` processes (PIDs 11389 and 11391). Their parent is PID 1, they were started at 22:52, they hold ports 4124 and 4161, and their working directory is `simple-dispatcher-workspaces/8f17b604-…/LinearViewer`, a workspace at `600f1be`. Settle it before merge: once those ports are free, run the system suite in A, B and C on the PR head and post the after-table. B's 12 file failures from the clone-root leak must be gone.
- **Inside, probable (only an actual host or location cause is in scope):** those orphaned servers look like a system-suite Harbour harness that a killed or timed-out run left behind (parent PID 1, a `main` checkout at the baseline commit, started during the baseline window). A stale server from an earlier run that makes clean `main` fail is a host-state cause of exactly the kind this ticket covers. Settle it before merge: confirm whether `test/system/harness/harbour.js` reaps its servers when the runner is killed or times out. If it does not, fix that here or drop it with the reason.
- **Inside (plan step 4, triage):** the 4 failures in A (`halt-mechanism`, `harbour-halt`, `observation-feed`, `tap1-openrouter`) were reported as "not triaged". The plan asked for one triage pass each: Harbour version mismatch, or an SD regression? Settle it before merge with that pass. Any cause that turns out not to be host or location gets a ticket, which is fine for that part.
- **Outside:** the real precondition branch (`faulted: true` → the probe must refuse) cannot run on this host, because git works here. Only the stubbed unit tests and M3 cover it. Settle it with a monitor already in place: the boot-time `gitLaunchProbe` refusal in production fails loudly on a host that has the shim fault.
- **Substitute limits:** my host runs share this machine's state, cover only `eb167d8` and its merge onto `0992f39`, and come from one run per location.

### Verdict
**Request Changes**: the D1 pin silently disables the LIN-558 clone-root guard, which the ticket forbids, and the system-suite after-table (plan step 4) is still missing. Next action: **implementation** on this task. Apply the `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT` fix and its witness, re-run the system suite in A, B and C once ports 4124–4161 are free, and check whether the harness leaves orphaned servers. The unit-suite parts (D2, D3, D4, and the D1 pin itself) are verified and need no changes.

**LIN-4181 revision: PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/309, pushed `4046a0d` on `feat/lin-4181-clean-main-test-run` (on top of `eb167d8`, no new PR).**

**CI: NOT green for `4046a0d`.** `ci.yml` runs on `pull_request`, but no run has registered for `4046a0d` about 15 minutes after the push; the only run is still `eb167d8` (success). CI exists, so the substitute does not apply. The CI gate is open until a run on `4046a0d` goes green.

**Findings → fixes**
- **F1 (blocking): the clone-root pin made the LIN-558 guard vacuous.** `test/workspace-clones.test.js` returned early whenever `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT` was set, and the preload always sets it. Fix: `config.js` exports `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`; the guard drops the early return and asserts that constant. Witness: with the default mutated to `<repo>/state/workspaces`, the guard is red under the preload and green once restored. Under full `npm test` with that mutation, two guards fail: the LIN-558 guard and `state-dir.test.js` (hard-coded `state/` in `config.js`).
- **F2 (system suite, orphaned servers): the harness never reaped Harbour.** Harbour was stopped only in `after`/`finally`. Experiment: when a test file times out, its spawned child keeps running, and once the file process ends it is reparented to pid 1. Fix: `test/system/harness/reap.js` tracks each Harbour child and kills it on `exit`, `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`; `harbour.js` tracks at spawn. Witness: `test/system/harness-reap.test.js`, red with the reaper stubbed (the child survives both exit and SIGTERM), green with it, and the exit case red with the exit handler disabled. **Limit:** a `SIGKILL` of the file process cannot be intercepted in-process; documented in `docs/testing-and-ci.md`.
- **Cleared orphans (disclosure):** on this host 8 `node server.js` processes (PIDs 11291, 11297, 11352, 11389, 11391, 11443, 11444, 11503) held ports 4124/4161. All had PPID 1, started 22:52, and ran from another workspace's LinearViewer clone (`8f17b604…`). That workspace had no other live process. They ignored SIGTERM and I SIGKILLed those eight PIDs. Ports are free and no `server.js` orphans remain.

**Unit suite `npm test` (commit `4046a0d`)**
| Location | Before (`eb167d8` per author) | After |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A. workspace clone, session TMPDIR | 3837, 0 fail, 5 skip | 3837, 0 fail, 5 skip, 0 leaks |
| B. clone under shared `/private/tmp`, per-user TMPDIR | 3837, 0 fail, 0 leaks (author) | 3837, 0 fail, 5 skip, 0 leaks |
| C. clone with TMPDIR inside `state/` | 3837, 0 fail (author) | 3837, 0 fail, 5 skip, 0 leaks |

The five skips each carry a reason, including the git-probe one: `login shell resolves git to /opt/homebrew/bin/git, which works; the Apple shim fault is not present on this host`. The 1/4/119 baseline from the planner's table is the pre-fix measurement, not repeated here.

**System suite `npm run test:system` (HARBOUR_DIR = LinearViewer at `10b2c82f`, the checkout on disk)**
| Location | Tests | Fail | Leaks |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A | 119 | 4 | 0 |
| B | 119 | 4 | 0 |
| C | 119 | 4 | 0 |

The count is 119 because the two reaper witnesses are new. The four failures are identical in all three locations: `halt-mechanism` (`follow-up still queued`), `harbour-halt` (`the follow-up is still queued, unclaimed`), `observation-feed` (`a completed run is not "in flight"`), `tap1-openrouter` (`a terminal run (loopId) materialized`). B went from 16 failures to 4 (the 12 clone-root file failures are gone), and C from unmeasured to 4.

**Triage of the four (step 4)**
- Same four on clean `main` (`0992f39`) with the same Harbour: not a branch regression.
- Same four with Harbour at the ticket's pinned `9e397e6b`: not Harbour-version skew.
- Same four in all three run locations: not host or location.
- So they are not host noise. Per the ticket, the tests are unchanged here. They are named as known failing. **Not yet ticketed**; one ticket per cause still needs filing.

**Still open, stated plainly**
- The real `faulted: true` branch of the git probe can't run on this host, since git works here. Only the stubbed unit cases and the mutation check cover it.
- CI on `4046a0d` not registered (above).

**Requesting re-review** on `4046a0d`. Please check the F1 witness (`test/workspace-clones.test.js` plus the `config.js` export) and the reaper witness (`test/system/harness-reap.test.js`).

**Autopilot note (CI gate diagnosis).** The missing CI run for `4046a0d` is not a GitHub trigger fault. PR #309 is `mergeable: CONFLICTING` / `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY` against `main` (`0992f39`, LIN-4180 #308); the branch is based on `600f1be`. GitHub does not start `pull_request` workflows on a conflicting PR, which is why only `eb167d8` has a run. The review's earlier clean-merge check predates the second push, so the conflict is most likely between the harness-reap change (`test/system/harness/harbour.js`) and LIN-4180's edit. Fix is on the branch, not a human gate: rebase or merge `main` into `feat/lin-4181-clean-main-test-run`, resolve keeping both changes, re-run the unit and system suites, push, and confirm CI actually registers and passes on the new head.

**LIN-4181 revision pushed: PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/309, head `63deab4` on `feat/lin-4181-clean-main-test-run` (no new PR).**

**CI: green on `63deab4`** (`unit tests`, run 41744445692, success). PR is `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN`. The conflict is resolved: a merge of `origin/main` (`0992f39`, LIN-4180) into the branch. The only conflict was `test/system/harness/harbour.js`, where both sides added an import line; both are kept (`trackChild` from the reaper, `locateHarbour` from LIN-4180). The reaper call site and `resolveHarbourDir()` both survive.

**Findings → fixes** (the review on `eb167d8` was Request Changes; the revision `4046a0d` already carried these, and this pass changed nothing in them)
- **F1 (LIN-558 guard vacuous):** `config.js` exports `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`; `test/workspace-clones.test.js` asserts that constant, with no early return. Witness from the revision: default mutated to `<repo>/state/workspaces` → guard red under the preload.
- **F2 (orphaned Harbour servers):** `test/system/harness/reap.js` kills each tracked Harbour child on `exit`/`SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`; witness `test/system/harness-reap.test.js`. Limit: `SIGKILL` of the runner cannot be intercepted; documented in `docs/testing-and-ci.md`.

**Unit suite `npm test` on `63deab4`**
| Location | Tests | Fail | Skip | Leaks |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A. workspace clone, session TMPDIR | 3859 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| B. checkout under `/tmp`, `TMPDIR=$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)` | 3859 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| C. checkout with TMPDIR inside its `state/` | 3859 | 0 | 5 | 0 |

Before (planner's baseline on `600f1be`): A 1 fail, B 4 fail + 704 leaks, C 119 fail + ~8900 leaks. The five skips each carry a reason; the git-probe one is `login shell resolves git to /opt/homebrew/bin/git, which works; the Apple shim fault is not present on this host`.

**System suite `npm run test:system` on `63deab4`** (Harbour `LinearViewer` @ `0dc1620e`, auto-discovered)
| Location | Tests | Fail | Leaks |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A | 119 | 4 | 0 |
| B | 119 | 4 | 0 |
| C | 119 | 4 | 0 |

Before: A 117 / 4 fail; B 129 / 16 fail (the 12 extra were whole files failing on the `/tmp` clone-root leak, now gone); C unmeasured on the planner's baseline.

The same four fail in all three locations: `halt-mechanism` (`follow-up still queued`), `harbour-halt` (`the follow-up is still queued, unclaimed`), `observation-feed` (`a completed run is not "in flight"`), `tap1-openrouter` (`a terminal run (loopId) materialized`).

**Triage of the four (plan step 4)**
- Not a branch regression: `origin/main` (`0992f39`) run with the same Harbour `0dc1620e` gives the same four in location B, plus the 12 `/tmp` clone-root file failures that the branch removes.
- Not Harbour-version skew: they also fail at Harbour `9e397e6b` (the ticket's pin) and `10b2c82f`.
- Not host or location: identical across A, B and C.
- So they are known failing, not host-related. Per the ticket, the tests are unchanged here. **Not yet ticketed**: one ticket per cause still needs filing once someone has the cause.

**Still open, stated plainly**
- The real `faulted: true` branch of the git probe can't run on this host (git works here). Only the stubbed unit cases and the mutation check cover it. A boot-time refusal in production is the monitor for that case.
- Substitute limits: all runs were on this one host and one run per location, so the numbers are not from an author-independent environment.

Requesting re-review on `63deab4`. The changes since `4046a0d` are the merge commit only; the conflict resolution is one import line.

## Review — LIN-4181

Re-review of PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/309, head `63deab4` (merge of `origin/main` `0992f39` into `4046a0d`). The PR is `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN`.

CI: green on `63deab4` (`unit tests`, run 41744445692, Linux). The system suite is not in CI (`ci.yml` runs `npm test` only). For that suite I re-ran the substitute myself on this host, PR head and `main`, and diffed failure names. Results below.

### Scope against the last review
The last review (on `eb167d8`) was Request Changes with one blocking finding and three inside ledger items. Since then the diff is `4046a0d` (F1 + F2) plus a merge commit. The merge resolution is one import line in `test/system/harness/harbour.js`: `trackChild` and LIN-4180's `locateHarbour` are both kept, and the `trackChild(child)` call site and `resolveHarbourDir()` both survive. Nothing goes beyond the plan, other than the reaper. The reaper was a ledger item from the last review (a host-state cause), so it is in scope.

### Checks I ran (Node v25.9.0, host git `/opt/homebrew/bin/git`)
- **F1, LIN-558 guard no longer vacuous.** `config.js` exports `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT`, and `test/workspace-clones.test.js` asserts it with no early return. **Mutation:** I set the default to `path.join(__dirname, 'state', 'workspaces')`, then ran the file under the preload (`WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT` pinned). The guard went red, 15 pass / 1 fail, and was green again once I reverted.
- **F2, reaper witness (`test/system/harness-reap.test.js`).** Baseline: 2/2 pass. Mutations, each reverted after:
  - M5: `reapAll` made a no-op. Both cases go red.
  - M6: `process.on('exit', reapAll)` removed. The exit case goes red and the SIGTERM case stays green.
  - M7: the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers removed. The SIGTERM case goes red and the exit case stays green.
  Each case catches exactly the path it names.
- **F2 wiring (no test covers this, so I checked by hand).** The witness only exercises `reap.js` on its own. Nothing in the suite would go red if `harbour.js` stopped calling `trackChild`. So I started a real Harbour with `startHarbour({port: 4199})` against `../LinearViewer` @ `0dc1620e`, then called `process.exit(0)` without calling `stop()`. Wired, the server is gone. With `trackChild(child)` commented out, the server **survives** (I killed it by hand afterwards). The wiring works.
- **Unit suite (`npm test`) at `63deab4`:**

| Location | tests | fail | skip | leaks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. workspace clone, session TMPDIR | 3859 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| B. `git clone --local` in `/private/tmp`, `TMPDIR=$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)` | 3859 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| C. TMPDIR inside the checkout's `state/` | 3859 | 0 | 5 | 0 |

  Every skip gives a reason (iTerm2 ×2, tmux, two unpinned contract cases, and the git probe: `login shell resolves git to /opt/homebrew/bin/git, which works; the Apple shim fault is not present on this host`).
- **System suite (`npm run test:system`, `HARBOUR_DIR` = `../LinearViewer` @ `0dc1620e`):**

| Run | tests | fail | leaks |
|---|---|---|---|
| A, `main` @ `0992f39` | 117 | 4 | 0 |
| A, PR @ `63deab4` | 119 | 4 | 0 |
| B, PR | 119 | 4 | 0 |
| C, PR | 119 | 4 | 0 |

  The failing test names are identical across all four runs: `halt-mechanism` (S3), `harbour-halt` (S4), `observation-feed`, and `tap1-openrouter`. The PR and `main` have the same names, so there is no regression. B and C have the same names as A, so these are not host or location effects. The two extra tests on the PR are the reaper witnesses. No `EADDRINUSE`, and no `node server.js` orphans remained after the runs.
- **Regression history.** Since the ticket was created, the only change to these files on `main` is LIN-4180 (`harbour.js`, Harbour discovery), and it is intact after the merge. The D1/D2/D3/D4 checks from the last review (M1–M4) still apply: none of that code changed after `eb167d8`.
- **One of a class?** The orphan-child class covers spawns the system harness makes. `harbour.js` is the only spawn in `test/system/harness/` and `test/system/*.test.js`. The runner `run-system.js` already forwards signals to its child. So the reaper covers the whole class today. The early-return-on-a-preload-env class was searched last round and found isolated. Nothing new here.
- **Nit (not blocking).** The header of `test/system/harness/reap.js` says it reaps "(Harbour servers, runners, fakes)", but only `harbour.js` calls `trackChild`. Close-out: change that parenthesis to "(today, the Harbour servers `harbour.js` starts; track any new harness spawn here too)".

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Outside (four system failures, triaged not host-related):** `halt-mechanism`, `harbour-halt`, `observation-feed` and `tap1-openrouter` fail the same on `main` and the PR, in A, B and C, and at Harbour `9e397e6b`, `10b2c82f` and `0dc1620e`. Per plan step 4 they are left unchanged here and are still **not ticketed**. Settle by a routed follow-up: close-out files one ticket per cause. If the cause is not yet known, file one ticket per failing file, stating the failing assertion and that it reproduces on clean `main` with every Harbour version tried. ## Survey 1a (round 3)

My pass was the last one: merge `main` into the branch, re-measure, post. So I mostly saw the end state.

**1. Why was this difficult?** My part wasn't. The conflict was one import line in `harbour.js`. The ticket as a whole got stuck in two places.
- **The shared test preload.** Any env var it pins reaches every test. Pinning `WORKSPACE_CLONE_ROOT` silently disabled the LIN-558 guard, which returned early on that variable. Nothing went red; review found it by mutation.
- **The system suite depends on host state.** Fixed ports 4124–4161 collided with orphaned servers. The Harbour checkout on disk also moved during the ticket (`9e397e6b` → `10b2c82f` → `0dc1620e`), so "same Harbour" was never held fixed.

The CI gap was hidden too. A conflicting PR starts no `pull_request` run, and the pass before mine read that as slow CI.

**2. What I'd have done first:** run `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus`. That was the real blocker, and one call shows it. I'd also record the Harbour commit up front.

**3. What I'd tidy:**
- Script the A/B/C baseline so it runs all three locations and diffs failure names. Done by hand, I got it slightly wrong: my `main` comparison ran in a `/tmp` worktree, picked up the clone-root leak, and I had to read around it.
- Give the system suite ephemeral ports, so orphans can't collide even after a `SIGKILL`.
- Ticket the four known-failing system tests.
- A correction: my Linear comment said the four "also fail at `9e397e6b` and `10b2c82f`". That came from the previous pass; I didn't re-run it. Nor did I re-run the F1/F2 witnesses. I should have marked both as inherited.

**4. What the ticket would have been:** If config exposed defaults apart from env-resolved values, the harness derived every path root from the run root in one place, and the system harness owned its ports and children, this ticket would have been "add the clone root to the run-root list", or nothing. The git-probe test would have been precondition-gated from the start.

**5. What the plan got wrong:**
- "Fits one session": it took three passes plus a conflict.
- Its "likeliest ways this breaks" missed that an env pin can make an existing guard vacuous. That was the one real defect.
- It guessed the four system failures "look like Harbour behaviour". Triage didn't bear that out, so the cause is still unknown.
- It named Harbour `9e397e6b` without pinning it, so later measurements drifted.

The "46" was rightly dropped as untraceable.
